scope_note: Comprehensive canon legislation file. Provisions marked [GENERATED] are plausible drafts consistent with canon intent; provisions marked [LOCKED] are established canon. Dates/votes marked null are not yet locked in canon.

legislation.name: We The People Act 1
legislation.key_effect: Early anti-corruption / money-in-politics reforms (baseline for later WTP stack).

provisions.text: Mandatory disclosure of all federal lobbying expenditures above $500.
2-year cooling-off period for executive branch officials before entering lobbying roles (revolving door restriction).
Public financing option for congressional campaigns via matching of small-dollar donations.
Caps on individual and PAC contributions to federal candidates.
Required disclosure of bundled campaign contributions and bundler identities.
Prohibited federal contractors from making campaign contributions during active contract periods.
Created an independent Office of Public Integrity within DOJ with subpoena power.
Strengthened whistleblower protections for federal employees reporting corruption.

notes: Details and vote counts not yet locked in canon; treated as enacted March 2001.

legislation.name: Rail Access, Intercity Linkage, and System Renewal Act
legislation.key_effect: Launches a 10-year national rail modernization program focused on the Northeast Corridor, California, Miami-Atlanta, and St. Louis-Chicago corridors, with all major works required to be compatible with future true high-speed rail.

provisions.text: Authorized $52 billion over 10 fiscal years for intercity passenger rail modernization, corridor development, and supporting manufacturing capacity.
Designated the Northeast Corridor, California Intercity Rail Program, the Miami-Atlanta Southeast Corridor, and the St. Louis-Chicago Midwest Corridor as Phase I priority corridors.

Required all federally funded corridor investments to be HSR-compatible where practical, including right-of-way preservation, curve easing, bridge/tunnel clearances, station throat design, and electrification geometry sufficient for later 186+ mph segments where feasible.

Created a Northeast Corridor Infrastructure Authority to coordinate Amtrak, FRA, commuter railroads, and affected states on shared capital sequencing, dispatch standards, and slot protection for intercity service.
Created a California Rail Compact grant program for Los Angeles-San Diego, Los Angeles-Bakersfield, San Jose-Sacramento, and San Francisco-Sacramento upgrades, with state matching funds required.

Created a Southeast Corridor Development Authority for Miami-Orlando-Jacksonville-Savannah-Atlanta, prioritizing new passenger-only segments where freight conflicts cannot be resolved cost-effectively.

Funded NEC state-of-good-repair and speed projects including catenary replacement, movable bridge renewal, interlocking reconstruction, power-supply upgrades, station throat modernization, and selective third/fourth tracking.

Funded California corridor projects including grade separations, double-tracking, curve modifications, signaling upgrades, electrification planning, and urban approach improvements to support frequent 110-125 mph service as the near-term standard.

Funded Miami-Atlanta projects including track rebuilding, grade crossing elimination, new bypasses around freight chokepoints, station redevelopment, and staged electrification beginning with the highest-frequency Florida segments.
Mandated nationwide deployment of cab signaling or positive train control equivalents on all Phase I passenger corridors by 2010 as a condition of continued federal capital support.
Authorized FRA to acquire, bank, and preserve right-of-way for future dedicated passenger alignments in constrained urban and suburban segments.

Established a rolling-stock and rail electrification manufacturing credit for firms opening or expanding U.S. plants producing trainsets, transformers, catenary hardware, signaling systems, and rail components.
Required project labor agreements or equivalent labor standards on major civil works and funded apprenticeship pipelines tied to rail construction, electrical work, dispatching, and maintenance.
Reformed Amtrak capital accounting by separating Northeast Corridor infrastructure accounts from national operating accounts to make reinvestment levels and corridor performance transparent.
Set corridor performance targets for trip-time reduction, frequency growth, on-time performance, and grade-crossing risk reduction, with biennial public reporting to Congress.

notes: Designed as a 2001-start modernization bill rather than an immediate full-HSR buildout; near-term operating target is mostly 110-125 mph outside the NEC, with corridor geometry and property acquisition intended to avoid foreclosing later dedicated HSR.
Political logic: sells as congestion relief, aviation resilience, manufacturing, and energy security, while embedding the legal and physical prerequisites for later true high-speed rail conversion.
The St. Louis-Chicago corridor was added to the program in 2004 due to its shorter projected time to completion.

legislation.name: Solar Energy Initiative Act of 2001
legislation.key_effect: Launched a national mobilization to make solar power the cheapest form of new energy generation, creating a domestic manufacturing base.

provisions.text: Established a national goal of achieving 90% cost reduction for utility-scale solar by 2015.
Authorized $50 billion in federal loan guarantees and grants for the construction of utility-scale solar farms and residential rooftop solar installations.
Created a Solar Manufacturing Investment Tax Credit to onshore the entire solar supply chain, from polysilicon to panel assembly.
Directed the Department of Energy to establish three National Solar Research Institutes focused on next-generation photovoltaic, storage, and grid integration technologies.
Mandated that all federal agencies source 30% of their electricity from renewable sources by 2012.
Integrated with the GridSmart program (est. 2003) to prioritize energy storage solutions and high-voltage direct current (HVDC) transmission corridors from high-production solar zones.

outcomes.as_of_2007: 340,000+ jobs in solar manufacturing; utility-scale solar cost achieved at $0.12/kWh.

notes: A major first-term climate and industrial policy initiative. The job creation and cost reduction figures are key administration talking points.

legislation.name: We The People Act 2
legislation.key_effect: Expanded anti-corruption, transparency, and enforcement regime (consolidated WTP2 and WTP3).

provisions.text: Extended WTP1 disclosure requirements to 501(c)(4) and (c)(6) dark money organizations spending on federal elections.
Required real-time (48-hour) electronic filing of all contributions over $1,000.
Mandated public disclosure of earmark sponsors in all appropriations legislation.
Required federal agencies to publish lobbying contact logs (who met with whom, when).
Expanded FOIA response timelines and created enforcement penalties for non-compliance.
Created a searchable public database consolidating campaign finance, lobbying, and contractor data.
Extended revolving-door restrictions to senior congressional staffers.
Prohibited use of official resources (staff, franking) for campaign activity.
Created a dedicated Public Corruption Strike Force within FBI, jointly supervised by the independent Office of Public Integrity.
Increased criminal penalties for bribery, honest-services fraud, and obstruction in federal corruption cases.
Authorized civil asset freezes pending corruption investigations without requiring criminal conviction.
Extended RICO applicability to public corruption schemes.
Mandated financial disclosures for all Senate-confirmed appointees, updated annually and publicly posted.
Established an independent Inspector General for the Office of Public Integrity itself.
Required federal courts to expedite corruption cases involving sitting officials.

notes: Consolidated transparency and enforcement stack (formerly WTP2 and WTP3).

legislation.name: PusheenCare Coverage Act
legislation.key_effect: Established a robust public option to close the coverage gap while maintaining the private insurance market.

provisions.text: Public option architecture enacted to close the coverage gap; very high public approval in-canon.
Established a federal baseline insurance plan available to all individuals currently in the 'coverage gap' (uninsured or underinsured).
Authorized employers to purchase PusheenCare coverage for their employees as a competitive alternative to private group plans.
Mandated that PusheenCare plans maintain actuarial value and provider networks sufficient to compete directly with top-tier private insurance.
Preserved the existing private insurance market, leaving private insurers mostly untouched and allowing them to continue offering supplemental and primary plans.
Utilized federal scale to negotiate provider reimbursement rates for the public option, ensuring cost-competitiveness with the private sector.

Empowered the Department of Health and Human Services to directly negotiate all prescription drug prices for the public option, establishing a 'most-favored-nation' price cap ensuring Americans never pay more than allied nations.
Provided federal subsidies for low-to-middle income individuals to purchase either PusheenCare or private plans through a national exchange.

Implemented a 'Benefit Pass-Through' requirement, mandating that any employer savings realized by switching from private plans to PusheenCare be redirected into employee base wages or supplemental health benefits.

notes: Core signature achievement; detailed statutory structure not fully itemized in source PDFs.

legislation.name: We The People Act 3 (Supreme Court Reform Act)
legislation.key_effect: Comprehensive reform of the Supreme Court and judicial nomination process.

provisions.text: Expanded the Supreme Court of the United States from 9 to 13 justices.
Established a mandatory, enforceable Code of Conduct for Supreme Court Justices, overseen by the Office of Public Integrity.
Created a non-partisan Judicial Nominating Commission to evaluate and recommend candidates for federal judicial vacancies.
Required the President to provide a formal written justification to the Senate for any judicial nomination made outside the Commission's recommended list.

notes: Redefined as the Supreme Court Reform Act following the consolidation of enforcement provisions into WTP2.

legislation.name: Universal Child Care Act of 2003
legislation.key_effect: Establishes a federal framework and funding for universal, affordable child care for all pre-kindergarten children.

provisions.text: Creates a system of federally-funded, locally-administered child care centers.
Caps parent co-pays based on a sliding income scale, with no family paying more than 7% of their income.
Establishes federal quality standards for child care providers, including staff-to-child ratios and educational requirements for staff.
Provides grants for the construction and expansion of child care facilities.

notes: Passed in 2003 as part of the administration's social policy agenda.

legislation.name: Universal School Lunch and Breakfast Act of 2003
legislation.key_effect: Provides free breakfast and lunch to all K-12 students in public schools, regardless of income.

provisions.text: Amends the National School Lunch Act to make breakfast and lunch universally free for all students.
Increases federal reimbursement rates to schools for meals served.
Establishes higher nutritional standards for school meals, emphasizing fresh fruits, vegetables, and whole grains.
Eliminates the application and verification process for free and reduced-price meals to reduce administrative burden and social stigma.

notes: Passed in 2003 to combat child hunger and improve educational outcomes.

legislation.name: GridSmart Modernization & Reliability Program
legislation.key_effect: Nationwide grid modernization; Puerto Rico treated as an early high-priority target due to systemic fragility.

dates.notes: Approximate; described as roughly 4 years old by 2007.

provisions.text: Puerto Rico designated as early high-priority target for grid hardening due to systemic fragility; improvements felt by 2007.
Established a federal Smart Grid Investment Office within DOE to coordinate and fund modernization grants.
Required all utilities serving over 100,000 customers to submit 10-year grid modernization plans within 18 months.
Authorized $40 billion in federal matching grants for smart meter deployment, automation, and substation hardening.
Mandated interoperability standards for all new grid equipment sold in the United States.
Created a Grid Reliability Corps within FEMA for rapid deployment of emergency grid restoration teams.
Required critical infrastructure nodes to have 72-hour backup power capability by 2008.

notes: Program framing: reliability, automation, hardening for critical infrastructure.

legislation.name: We The People Act 4
legislation.key_effect: Beneficial ownership / transparency stack becomes strong enough to make later asset freezes feasible in real time.

provisions.text: Beneficial ownership disclosure requirements strengthened to enable real-time asset freeze capability.
Financial transparency provisions sufficient to make Sackler-family asset freeze feasible in canon.
Money flow visibility requirements enabling active federal investigation and interdiction.
Required all federally chartered LLCs, corporations, and statutory trusts to file beneficial ownership disclosures with FinCEN.

Expanded FinCEN beneficial ownership database to include all entities with gross revenues over $50,000 annually, utilizing a tiered reporting system where entities under $500,000 gross revenue may utilize a 'Simplified Beneficial Ownership' (SBO) disclosure.
Required beneficial ownership updates within 30 days of any ownership change.
Authorized Treasury to issue emergency asset freeze orders for entities under active corruption or money-laundering investigation, effective within 24 hours.
Created cross-agency data-sharing protocols linking FinCEN, IRS, DOJ, and the Office of Public Integrity.
Prohibited use of shell company chains exceeding two layers for federal contracting purposes.
Mandated the adoption of Global Legal Entity Identifiers (LEI) for all entities filing beneficial ownership disclosures to ensure unique identification across datasets.
Required the Office of Public Integrity to establish a real-time, encrypted API for automated data exchange with Tier-1 financial institutions to support 24-hour interdiction capability.
Established a 'Due Process Safeguard' requiring a mandatory judicial review hearing within 72 hours of any emergency asset freeze order issued under this Act.

notes: Canon implication: WTP4 beneficial-ownership requirements enable Sackler asset freeze and visibility of money flows.

legislation.name: Auto-Filled Returns Implementation Act
legislation.key_effect: IRS auto-filled returns implemented a few years before 2007; very popular in-canon.

provisions.text: IRS authorized and directed to auto-fill federal tax returns for eligible filers using W-2, 1099, and third-party data.
Filers with income solely from wages, interest, and dividends receive pre-filled returns by March 1 each year.
Filers may accept auto-filled return, amend online, or opt out entirely; acceptance requires one confirmation action.
IRS prohibited from contracting with private tax preparation software companies in ways that restrict access to auto-fill.
Free federal filing portal mandated for all taxpayers regardless of income.
Auto-fill program phased in over 3 years; initially available to filers with adjusted gross income under $150,000.

notes: Exact year not locked; placed 2004 consistent with 'implemented a few years ago' framing from 2007 canon.

legislation.name: America First Forever Act
legislation.key_effect: Creates durable trust funds and survivability mechanics for core delivery programs.

provisions.text: Establishes durable trust funds for health, rural opportunity, community development, coal transition, and veterans programs.
Established a 2-year pilot program funded at $1 million per day to capitalize the trust funds.
Following the pilot program, capitalization is set at 10% of the annual federal budget surplus, beginning in FY2007.
Trust fund principal protected by supermajority (67 Senate votes) requirement for drawdown or rescission.
Independent Trust Fund Oversight Board with 10-year staggered terms; removable only for cause.
Annual actuarial review published publicly; automatic trigger adjustments if trust fund solvency falls below 20-year horizon.
Programs funded from trust funds exempted from annual appropriations process; governed by standing authorizations.

notes: Referenced in campaign file with trust fund structure; vote counts not in source snippet.

legislation.name: Digital Accountability and Transparency in Advertising and Data Act
legislation.key_effect: Establishes a national data broker registry, imposes an excise tax on data sales, and creates strict consent requirements for personal data.

provisions.text: Requires all entities that sell, rent, or trade personal data to register with a new federal Transparency Registry.
Mandates registered data brokers to disclose categories of data collected, data sources, and categories of data buyers.
Imposes a significant excise tax (10x baseline proposal) on the commercial sale or rental of user data.
Requires explicit opt-in consent from consumers before their personal data can be sold.
Establishes a 'sensitive data' category including health, financial, and location information, requiring consent via certified mail for initial sale and annual renewal.
Grants consumers the right to see what data a broker holds on them, request its deletion, and prohibit its sale.
Applies to data brokers, advertising networks, and large digital platforms like search and social media.
Establishes criminal liability for the knowing misuse of sensitive data or intentional failure to disclose data sales.

notes: Established the public Transparency Registry at www.iamashill.gov.
A key part of the administration's consumer protection and anti-corruption agenda.
The 10x multiplier on the data sales excise tax was a late addition during negotiations, significantly strengthening the bill's deterrent effect.

legislation.name: We The People Act 5
legislation.key_effect: Further closes dark-money channels; strengthens enforcement posture going into 2006–2007 prosecutions.

provisions.text: Closed remaining 501(c)(6) trade association dark-money loopholes not addressed in WTP2.
Required online political advertising to carry real-time donor disclosure at point of display.
Extended civil RICO provisions to coordinated dark-money networks, requiring that any associated asset restraining orders adhere to the 72-hour judicial review hearing mandated in WTP4.
Increased maximum sentences for conviction under WTP1–4 enforcement provisions.
Created a Corruption Asset Recovery Fund, directing proceeds from forfeiture actions into public campaign finance matching pool.

Empowered the Office of Public Integrity to initiate investigations without referral from executive branch agencies, ensuring all resulting emergency interdictions are gated by the WTP4 Due Process Safeguard.
Mandated annual public reporting by DOJ on all pending and resolved public corruption prosecutions.

Expanded the definition of 'lobbying activity' to include 'strategic policy consulting,' requiring registration for any individual or entity receiving over $2,500 per quarter to influence federal policy, regardless of direct contact with officials.

notes: Not fully itemized in original canon files; provisions generated consistent with enforcement escalation arc.

legislation.name: We The People Act 6
legislation.key_effect: House expansion for the original 50 states to 1,000 seats and related election-administration modernization. Seats for new states are added on top of this number.

implementation_defaults.districts: States may retain pre-WTP6 districts for legacy seats.
implementation_defaults.at_large_expansion_seats: New seats created by expansion may be elected at-large with one additional at-large vote per voter; top X vote-getters win X at-large seats (SNTV).
implementation_defaults.at_large_ballot_rule: Candidate-choice only for at-large (no straight-ticket) per House Admin guidance (not new legislation).

provisions.text: House of Representatives for the original 50 states expanded from 435 to 1,000 seats.
Representation for new states admitted to the Union is calculated and added on top of the 1,000 seats apportioned to the original 50 states.
New expansion seats may be elected at-large using Single Non-Transferable Vote (SNTV); top vote-getters fill available seats.
States may retain pre-WTP6 district boundaries for legacy seats.
McMillan Complex authorized as purpose-built House chamber.
Congressional apportionment formula recalculated using cube-root rule as population baseline for legacy seat allocation.
Required ranked-choice voting for all single-member House districts in states with at least 5 legacy seats.
Established federal minimum election administration standards (paper ballots, audit trails, uniform polling hours).
Automatic voter registration triggered by any interaction with federal agencies (SSA, IRS, USPS, DMV data-share).

Established expedited judicial review protocols, granting the Supreme Court original jurisdiction over challenges to the 1,000-seat apportionment and the validity of SNTV/RCV implementation to ensure representation is not delayed by litigation.

notes: Exact enactment date/votes not locked in current files.
McMillan Complex is the purpose-built House chamber (operational consequence of WTP6).
The complex was completed in January 2007, in time for the first session of the 110th Congress, though final landscaping was still in progress.

legislation.name: Financial Stability Act of 2005
legislation.key_effect: Pre-emptive regulation of subprime mortgage markets and over-the-counter derivatives to prevent systemic collapse.

provisions.text: Established federal anti-predatory lending standards, prohibiting 'exploding' ARMs and requiring documented verification of a borrower's ability to repay.
Imposed a hard national usury cap of 36% APR on all consumer lending, explicitly dismantling the payday loan and predatory title-loan industries.
Mandated that all over-the-counter (OTC) derivatives be traded on regulated exchanges and cleared through central counterparties to eliminate 'wild west' shadow markets.
Required mortgage securitizers to retain 5% of the credit risk ('skin in the game') for any asset-backed security issued.
Empowered the Office of Public Integrity and Treasury to set counter-cyclical capital requirements for Tier-1 financial institutions.
Prohibited federally insured depository institutions from engaging in proprietary trading of high-risk synthetic derivatives.
Created a National Mortgage Registry linked to the WTP4 beneficial ownership database to ensure real-time visibility of underlying asset ownership.

notes: Enacted to mitigate the emerging subprime bubble; leverages WTP4 infrastructure for real-time tracking of financial flows.

legislation.name: National High-Speed Rail Act of 2006
legislation.key_effect: Establishes a permanent, trust-fund-backed national HSR program and a government-owned TBM fleet to accelerate construction.

provisions.text: Adopts the US High-Speed Rail Association (USHSR) vision as the framework for a national HSR network.
Authorizes a new 10-year rolling budget for HSR construction, with funding automatically renewing each fiscal year unless explicitly voted to stop by Congress.
Establishes the High-Speed Rail Trust Fund to provide a dedicated, long-term funding source for the program.
Imposes a new federal excise tax on commercial airline fuel to capitalize the High-Speed Rail Trust Fund.
Upgrades the original RAILS corridors (NEC, California, Southeast, Midwest) to full HSR build-out specifications (220 mph target speeds).
Authorizes planning and construction for new Phase II corridors, including Texas Triangle (Dallas-Houston-Austin) and Cascadia (Eugene-Seattle-Vancouver).
Established the National Tunneling Authority (NTA), a government-owned corporation, to acquire, maintain, and operate a strategic fleet of Tunnel Boring Machines (TBMs).
Authorized the initial purchase of six (6) large-diameter TBMs, designating the Hudson Gateway Program as the first priority project.
Established a national training center for TBM operation and maintenance in partnership with labor unions and engineering schools.

notes: A major second-term infrastructure initiative that transitions from modernization to a full HSR buildout, creating a permanent funding mechanism and a national TBM fleet to accelerate construction.

legislation.name: Communications Evidence Preservation Act
legislation.key_effect: Provider-side retention of email traffic transiting major hubs; access only via warrant; privacy advocate attached to each warrant request.

provisions.text: Email service providers and carriers must retain traffic metadata transiting major hubs for 18 months.
Retained communications accessible only via warrant issued by Article III court.
A privacy advocate appointed to each warrant request, with standing to oppose issuance.
Providers must store retained data in encrypted form; decryption keys held by provider, not government.
Warrant applications must specify target, scope, and time window; general or dragnet warrants prohibited.
Annual public reporting required from DOJ on number of CEPA warrants issued, contested, and denied.
Civil liability established for unauthorized government access to CEPA-retained data.

notes: Introduced Jan 6, signed Jan 22, 2007. Exact vote counts not locked.

legislation.name: Gulf War Illness Recognition & Benefits Act
legislation.key_effect: Presumptive service-connection framework and benefits improvements for Gulf War illness.

provisions.text: Presumptive service-connection established for Gulf War illness; veterans need not prove specific exposure event.
Survivor benefit claims simplified for Gulf War illness fatalities.
VA directed to establish specialized Gulf War illness treatment centers at 12 regional facilities.
Research appropriation of $500 million over 5 years for Gulf War illness etiology and treatment studies.
Disability rating minimums established for qualifying Gulf War illness diagnoses.
Retroactive benefits available to veterans whose prior claims were denied on service-connection grounds.

notes: Passed alongside CEPA by Jan 22 per canon; exact vote counts not locked.

legislation.name: Make America Great Again — All of It Act
legislation.key_effect: Rural infrastructure omnibus; direct delivery support for non-urban America.

provisions.text: Rural infrastructure omnibus covering hospitals, broadband, roads, and energy.
Announced at SOTU January 23; submitted to Congress January 24.
Authorized $80 billion over 8 years in rural hospital construction, expansion, and stabilization grants.
Rural broadband connectivity mandate: universal access at minimum 25 Mbps by 2010 via AmeriSat and terrestrial co-investment.
Created a Rural Opportunity Fund providing low-interest loans for small businesses in counties with population under 50,000.
Funded 50,000 miles of rural road and bridge rehabilitation over 5 years.
Coal community transition grants providing retraining, relocation assistance, and economic diversification funding.
Funded through direct federal appropriations over an 8-year authorization period.

notes: Announced at SOTU Jan 23; introduced Jan 24. Passage date and vote counts not yet in canon.

legislation.name: Make America Tax Free / Tax Fairness and Work Rewarding Act
legislation.key_effect: 0% federal income tax rate on work income under thresholds; phase-in above; closes major high-end loopholes.

locked_parameters.before_after_notice_baseline: Use taxpayer's 2006 actual taxes as the 'before' baseline.

provisions.text: 0% federal income tax on work income up to $100k single / $200k joint / $150k head of household (inflation-indexed).
Graduated phase-in from threshold to $400k single / $800k joint / $600k head of household.
Senate vote: 62-38; House vote: 631-369.
Sponsored by Sen. Kennedy (Senate) and Rep. Conyers (House).
Carried interest loophole eliminated; private equity profits taxed as ordinary income.
Step-up in basis at death eliminated for estates over $5 million; unrealized gains taxed at transfer.
Offshore profit-shifting restrictions: U.S. corporations taxed on global income with credit for foreign taxes paid.
Capital gains rate harmonized with ordinary income rates above $1 million annual income.
IRS enforcement funding doubled; mandatory audit rate restored for high-income returns.
Established a 50:1 executive-to-median-worker compensation ratio, enforced via loss of deductibility and tiered excise taxes for non-compliant firms.
Corporate Minimum Tax: Imposed a 20% minimum tax on 'book income' for corporations with annual profits exceeding $1 billion.
Financial Transaction Tax: Imposed a 0.1% tax on stock trades and a 0.01% tax on derivative contracts to reduce high-frequency churn.
Stock Buyback Excise Tax: Imposed a 4% excise tax on corporate share repurchases to encourage reinvestment in labor and R&D.
Ultra-Wealth Tax: Established a 2% annual tax on net worth exceeding $100 million, utilizing WTP4 beneficial ownership data for valuation.
Mark-to-Market for Billionaires: Required annual taxation of unrealized capital gains for households with net worth exceeding $1 billion.
Reformed the estate tax with a 20% rate on assets between $5 million and $20 million, and a 77% rate on all assets exceeding $20 million.
1031 Exchange Limitation: Capped the deferral of capital gains on 'like-kind' real estate exchanges at $1,000,000 per year and eliminated the 25% recapture preference.
Private Jet & Luxury Fuel Surcharge: Imposed a 20% surcharge on non-commercial aviation fuel and luxury aircraft acquisitions.
Interest Deduction Cap: Limited corporate interest expense deductions to 30% of EBITDA to discourage high-leverage private equity buyouts.
Check-the-Box Loophole Closure: Prohibited the use of 'disregarded entity' status for offshore subsidiaries to hide passive income.
Refundable Child Tax Credit: Expanded the credit to $3,600 per child, made fully refundable and paid monthly.
EITC Expansion: Increased the Earned Income Tax Credit for childless workers and expanded eligibility to workers aged 19–70.
Standard Deduction Inflation-Indexing: Mandated annual adjustments to the 0% work-income floor to maintain purchasing power.
Education & Vocational Credit: Established a fully refundable credit for tuition and supplies for accredited trade schools and public universities.
Social Security Trust Fund Backfill: Authorized direct federal transfers to Social Security to offset revenue lost from low-income payroll tax exemptions.
FBAR Real-Time Reporting: Mandated 24-hour electronic reporting of foreign financial accounts with balances exceeding $50,000.
Tax Haven Contract Prohibition: Prohibited federal agencies from awarding contracts to entities utilizing non-cooperative tax jurisdictions.
Corporate Tax Whistleblower Bounty: Established a 30% reward for individuals providing evidence leading to the recovery of over $5 million in unpaid corporate taxes.
High-Value Asset Transfer Reporting: Required real-time disclosure of all non-currency asset transfers (art, real estate, equity) exceeding $1 million.
Luxury Goods Excise: Imposed a 10% surcharge on jewelry, yachts, and high-end vehicles with a retail price exceeding $150,000.
Shadow Lobbying Deduction Elimination: Prohibited corporations from deducting fees paid for 'strategic consulting' or 'policy advisory' services.
Global Minimum Tax Enforcement: Authorized the Treasury to impose 'top-up' taxes on U.S. entities operating in jurisdictions with effective rates below 15%.
Established a 'reasonable compensation' floor for materially participating owners of S-corps and partnerships to prevent avoidance of payroll taxes.
Tightened the 'Real Estate Professional' exception for passive loss rules, requiring 1500 hours minimum and contemporaneous records.
Instituted a Carbon Tax starting at $25/ton, with all initial proceeds returned via a per-capita dividend; tax rate scheduled to increase annually.
Pass-through Loss Limitation: Capped the deduction of pass-through business losses against non-business income at $500,000 annually.
Pass-through Retained Earnings Rule: Treated retained earnings beyond reasonable business needs as a deemed distribution for tax purposes.
Buyback Recharacterization: Recharacterized stock buyback proceeds as ordinary dividend income for tax purposes to remove preferential treatment.

notes: Vote counts locked. Announced SOTU Jan 23; introduced Jan 24.

legislation.name: Senate Filibuster Reform Act
legislation.key_effect: Removes/neutralizes the filibuster as a procedural weapon for blocking the agenda.

provisions.text: Filibuster eliminated or neutralized as a blocking mechanism; passes Senate 61-39 with 4 Democratic defections.
Cloture threshold reduced from 60 to simple majority (51) for all legislation and nominations.
Talking filibuster requirement reinstated as transition measure: any delay requires continuous floor presence.
Post-cloture debate time reduced from 30 hours to 2 hours for most legislation.
Unanimous consent calendar reforms to accelerate non-controversial nominations.

notes: Senate vote locked at 61-39 with 4 Democratic defections. House vote not specified in canon.

legislation.name: Washington Douglass Commonwealth Admission Act
legislation.key_effect: Creates Douglass Commonwealth by retroceding everything except a small federal enclave; grants full representation to ~700k residents.

provisions.text: Retrocedes all District territory except a small federal enclave (Capitol, White House, National Mall) to create the State of Douglass Commonwealth.
Grants full congressional representation to approximately 700,000 residents.
Senate vote: 63-37; House margin described as comfortable.
Convention-to-ratification-to-seating timeline approximately 6 months from enactment.
New state immediately entitled to 2 senators and House seats apportioned under WTP6.
Federal enclave retains name 'District of Columbia' for constitutional compliance; governed by joint Congressional committee.
Douglass Commonwealth state constitution ratified by existing DC Council acting as provisional convention.
Federal employees residing in new state retain federal employment rights; no double-taxation provision.

notes: Senate vote locked. House margin comfortable but not numerically specified. Seating ~6 months post-enactment.

legislation.name: Puerto Rico Status Referendum Act
legislation.key_effect: Federally administered, DOJ-overseen binding referendum within 60 days (ranked choice; trilingual ballots).

provisions.text: Federally administered, DOJ-overseen binding referendum to be held within 60 days of enactment.
Trilingual ballots (English, Spanish, and Puerto Rican Spanish variants).
Original statute provides 3-option ranked choice ballot; later canon discussion moved toward binary — not yet resolved.
Options: (1) Statehood, (2) Enhanced Commonwealth, (3) Independence.
DOJ Civil Rights Division designated as lead administrator; independent international observers invited.
Result binding on Congress; implementing legislation required within 90 days of certified result.
Campaign finance rules applied to referendum advocacy; foreign contributions prohibited.

notes: 3-option RCV is the statutory baseline per source PDF; binary option discussed but not locked as replacement.

legislation.name: Puerto Rico Admission Act of 2007
legislation.key_effect: Admits Puerto Rico as a state on equal footing; continuity-first transition.

provisions.text: Puerto Rico admitted as the 52nd state on equal footing with all existing states.
Target admission date October 1, 2007.
House delegation design aligns to Puerto Rico senatorial districts plus at-large seats under WTP6.
Smooth passage assumed in canon; exact vote counts to be filled once floor votes occur.
Commonwealth government, laws, and debts carry over; Puerto Rico Supreme Court decisions retained as binding precedent.
PusheenCare and all federal programs extended immediately; phase-in schedule for tax obligations over 5 years.
Spanish designated as co-official language for federal interactions within Puerto Rico.
Jones Act phase-in reform tied to PR admission; maritime restrictions relaxed for PR-origin vessels.

notes: Introduced May 20, 2007. Smooth passage assumed.

legislation.name: AmeriSat Act (Government-Owned LEO Satellite Internet Utility)
legislation.key_effect: Government-owned LEO constellation; U.S. rural users as priority; hybrid retail model.

provisions.text: Government-owned 1,200-satellite LEO constellation authorized.
Total capex $20 billion; deployment window 2009-2013.
Annual opex $1-2 billion; international licensing revenue projected at $4-8 billion annually.
Block 0 first light targeted 12-14 months from procurement start.
Hybrid retail model: direct service plus co-ops and resellers.
Rural U.S. users receive service at cost; urban users at market rate; cross-subsidy model codified.
AmeriSat designated as utility; open-access requirement for government data and emergency communications.
International licensing managed by State Department with revenue flowing to AmeriSat Operating Trust.
Procurement administered by NASA in partnership with DOD; launch manifest shared with existing contractors.

notes: Passed with strong bipartisan support following the successful passage of the SpaceX Integration Act. The bill was framed as a critical infrastructure and jobs program for rural America.

legislation.name: SpaceX Strategic Integration and Launch Competitiveness Act
legislation.key_effect: Authorizes the acquisition of SpaceX and its integration into NASA as a new launch services division with a ring-fenced Mars development program.

provisions.text: Authorizes the Administrator of NASA to acquire all assets, intellectual property, and liabilities of Space Exploration Technologies Corp. (SpaceX).
Establishes the 'NASA Launch Services Directorate' to be headquartered at the existing SpaceX campus in Hawthorne, CA, preserving the existing engineering and manufacturing teams.
Creates the position of 'Chief Visioneer and Director of Mars Development,' appointing Elon Musk to the role with final engineering authority over the Mars transportation architecture.

Establishes the Mars Development Program as a ring-fenced entity within the new directorate, with a dedicated 10-year, $20 billion appropriation for the development of the Mars Colonial Transporter (MCT) and supporting technologies.
Appropriates $100 million for the acquisition of SpaceX assets and the assumption of its liabilities.

notes: Passed after a brief but intense legislative battle. The administration successfully framed the bill as a strategic investment in competition and innovation, overcoming opposition from incumbent aerospace contractors.

legislation.name: Merchant Marine / Maritime Modernization Act
legislation.key_effect: Modernization of merchant marine / maritime capability.

provisions.text: Senate vote: 71-28 on November 28, 2007.
Authorized $15 billion shipbuilding investment fund for U.S.-flagged commercial and dual-use vessels.
Jones Act reformed: phase-in of domestic-build requirements for new vessel classes; existing fleet grandfathered.
Maritime workforce training program established via partnership with maritime academies.
U.S.-flagged fleet required for carriage of all federally financed cargo (food aid, military logistics).
Port modernization grants for top 20 U.S. ports; intermodal connectivity requirements.
Strategic Sealift Reserve expanded; minimum U.S.-flagged dry cargo capacity requirements set by DOD.

notes: Senate vote locked. House vote and signing date not specified in source.

legislation.name: Citizens United Democracy Act (Amendment Vehicle)
legislation.key_effect: Democracy reform amendment vehicle; includes Electoral College reform and campaign finance architecture.

provisions.text: Constitutional amendment vehicle covering Electoral College reform and campaign finance.
Electoral College reformed: faithless elector prohibited; presidential election determined by national popular vote compact enshrined constitutionally.
All independent expenditures over $1,000 in connection with federal elections require immediate public disclosure.
Foreign nationals and foreign-controlled entities prohibited from any participation in federal, state, or local elections.
Congress empowered to set aggregate contribution and expenditure limits without judicial strict scrutiny.

notes: Detailed titles exist in campaign file; exact vote counts not in source. Preceded by strategic WTP9 failure vote.

legislation.name: Voting Rights Forever Amendment
legislation.key_effect: Affirmative right to vote in federal elections; constitutionalized preclearance; private right of action; federal election standards floor.

provisions.text: Affirmative constitutional right to vote in federal elections for all citizens 18 and older.
Preclearance requirement constitutionalized with objective coverage triggers (not legislative discretion).
Private right of action established for voting rights violations.
Federal election standards floor created for federal elections only.
Senate vote: 69-31.
Objective preclearance triggers: jurisdictions with documented voter suppression incidents in prior 10 years, or statistical disparities in turnout above defined threshold.
Federal minimum standards: paper ballot requirement, 15 days early voting, same-day registration, polling place density minimums.
Attorney General empowered to seek injunctive relief for violations without showing of discriminatory intent (effects test constitutionalized).

notes: Passage paved by the failure of the omnibus WTP9.

legislation.name: American Democracy Act (Omnibus Statement Vehicle)
legislation.key_effect: Strategic omnibus combining WTP7+WTP8; intended to fail on first vote to create political record, then split.

provisions.text: Omnibus vehicle combining full text of WTP7 and WTP8.
Strategic intent: WTP9 voted first and allowed to fail, creating political record of opposition votes; WTP7 and WTP8 then pass separately.
Floor managers acknowledged omnibus nature in debate record, establishing legislative history for subsequent split bills.

notes: Status is 'unknown'/failed by design. Its failure is the prerequisite for WTP7 and WTP8 passage.

legislation.name: Real-Time Reality Act
legislation.key_effect: Establishes the Federal Integrity Commission (FIC) to enforce fiscal penalties against coordinated financial misinformation.

provisions.text: Establishes the Federal Integrity Commission (FIC) as an independent regulatory agency to combat coordinated financial misinformation.
Mandates the FIC be composed of 4 former Article III judges, 4 forensic accountants, and 4 data scientists, with 10-year staggered terms and a partisan cap.
Empowers the FIC to trigger an automatic IRS forensic audit of any entity it determines has engaged in a 'High Probability of Intentional Deception' in political advertising.
Imposes a 'Deception Tax,' an excise surcharge of 50% of a deceptive campaign's total budget, with revenue allocated to the Corruption Asset Recovery Fund.
Authorizes the FIC to order a 24-hour 'Account Interdiction' (freeze) on funding channels used for active misinformation campaigns, subject to mandatory judicial review within 72 hours.
Establishes a citizen filing process with a $1,000 'Bad Faith Deposit' to prevent harassment, initiating an FIC staff analysis of a claim's factual consistency using the Restore.gov API.
Creates an independent Privacy Advocate role within the FIC to challenge proposed interdictions and protect due process.

Requires digital platforms to integrate the 'One-Click Truth' Verification API and 'Live Donor Tooltips' for all advertising content that meets the standards for 'paid political and issue-based advertising' as defined by the independent Digital Speech and Transparency Council.

notes: The capstone of the WTP legislative stack, shifting focus from government transparency to the integrity of the information ecosystem.
Passage was secured by the 'Systems Caucus' of moderate House Republicans, who provided the bipartisan cover needed to overcome fierce opposition from the 'Anti-System' wing.

legislation.name: Social Media Contract with America
legislation.key_effect: Comprehensive regulation of digital platforms, establishing algorithmic transparency, data portability, user protections, and funding for public interest media.

provisions.text: Mandates algorithmic transparency, requiring platforms to disclose the variables and weights used in content recommendation systems to the Federal Integrity Commission (FIC).
Requires platforms to provide a reverse-chronological feed as the default user experience, with algorithmic curation strictly requiring explicit user opt-in.
Establishes strict data portability and interoperability standards, allowing users to seamlessly migrate their social graph and content between competing platforms.
Authorizes federal grants through the National Science Foundation (NSF) to support the research and development of decentralized, open-source social networking protocols.
Establishes a voluntary, privacy-preserving Universal Digital ID framework integrated with Restore.gov to authenticate human users and combat bot networks.
Mandates 'Well-Being by Design' principles, prohibiting infinite scrolling, dark patterns, and gamified engagement loops designed to foster behavioral addiction.
Expands the 2005 DATA Act to cover generative AI models, biometric inferences, and predictive behavioral profiling, requiring explicit affirmative consent for these new data risks.
Imposes strict anti-trust rules prohibiting dominant digital platforms from acquiring nascent competitors ('kill-zone acquisitions') or preferencing their own vertical services.
Prohibits all forms of targeted advertising and algorithmic profiling directed at users under the age of 18.
Revises platform liability shields, establishing legal accountability for platforms that algorithmically amplify illegal content, non-consensual deepfakes, or coordinated incitement to violence.

Imposes a progressive Digital Ad Revenue Tax on platforms with over 50 million users to fund the 'Public Interest Media Trust,' supporting local journalism, digital literacy education, and public broadcasting.
Directs portions of the Digital Ad Revenue Tax to aggressively fund independent, non-partisan fact-checking organizations and academic research into misinformation vectors.
Revises the Communications Act of 1934 to limit the number of broadcast licenses a single entity can own in a local media market, promoting diverse media ownership.
Creates a 'Community Media Voucher' program that provides seed funding for community-owned media outlets and news cooperatives.
Establishes a 'Public Media Archive' to preserve and promote access to local news content, counteracting the dominance of national news cycles.
Requires algorithmic transparency to focus on amplifying diverse voices.
Revises existing laws to place an emphasis on how algorithms prioritize content from local news sources and independent journalists. Provides grants to support local reporting initiatives.
Encourages media outlets to have employee ownership plans to better reinvest in local communities.
Mandates a full compensation and race and ethics breakdown for media corporations with more than 50 employees for compliance and transparency reasons. Will be actively monitored by FIC.
Provides financial support to independent and local media production companies. Subsidies can be obtained with a vote from a panel and demonstration of community need.
Allows public feedback with all claims of censorship or manipulation actively reviewed and investigated.
Requires clear labeling for automated accounts and content generated by AI.
Empowers the Federal Integrity Commission (FIC) to make assessments on any mergers that unduly harm competition.
Authorizes low-interest federal loans to local groups.
Restricts foreign governments, individuals, or entities from owning or controlling more than 25% of the voting stock of national media companies.

notes: Proposed as a flagship piece of legislation for the early Kang administration to regulate the emerging Web 2.0 and social media landscape.
Addresses the systemic incentive structures of digital platforms, extending the administration's 'Systems Integrity' agenda beyond traditional campaign finance.

legislation.name: Leveraging Investment for Future Talent Act
legislation.key_effect: Restructures federal student loan system, emphasizes financial controls and outcome based models

items: Mandatory Debt Sustainability Certification
Commercial loan refinancing into NEB accounts
Institutional tuition caps indexed to CPI
Universal Community College Grant Program
National Common Course Numbering (NCCN) for 100% transferability
Pell Grant flexibility for housing and childcare
Institutional subsidies tied to graduation metrics
5-year 100% debt forgiveness for high-need public service
Micro-service tuition vouchers for active students

Stringent regulations and oversight to prevent 'certificate mills' from exploiting the system. Institutions found to be primarily awarding certificates without demonstrable job placement outcomes will be ineligible for federal student loan programs.
Clear guidelines for the National Education Board (NEB) to determine eligible service areas for loan forgiveness programs. The NEB will prioritize areas based on the following criteria:
1. Underserved Communities:
a. Poverty Rate: Areas with poverty rates exceeding the national average will receive higher priority.
b. Lack of Access to Services: Communities lacking adequate access to healthcare, education, and other essential public services will be prioritized.
c. Geographic Isolation: Rural and remote areas with limited economic opportunities will be given special consideration.
d. Historical Disadvantage: Areas with a history of systemic discrimination and economic disinvestment will be prioritized to promote equity.
2. Critical Workforce Shortages:
a. Healthcare: Areas with a shortage of healthcare professionals, particularly in primary care and mental health, will be prioritized.
b. Education: Communities with a lack of qualified teachers, especially in STEM fields and special education, will receive higher consideration.
c. Public Safety: Areas with shortages of law enforcement officers, firefighters, and emergency medical personnel will be prioritized.
d. Infrastructure: Communities with a need for skilled workers in infrastructure development and maintenance, such as engineers and technicians, will be given priority.

e. Data-Driven Assessment: The NEB will use data from the Bureau of Labor Statistics and other relevant sources to identify specific workforce shortages in different regions and tailor loan forgiveness programs accordingly.
3. Additional Considerations:
a. Alignment with State and Local Needs: The NEB will coordinate with state and local governments to ensure that loan forgiveness programs align with regional economic development strategies.

b. Community Input: The NEB will solicit input from community stakeholders, including residents, employers, and educational institutions, to ensure that loan forgiveness programs are responsive to local needs.

c. Program Evaluation: The NEB will regularly evaluate the effectiveness of loan forgiveness programs in addressing underserved communities and critical workforce shortages, making adjustments as needed to maximize impact.

legislation.name: Trinity Technology Act
legislation.key_effect: Authorizes the $265B federal acquisition of Google, Apple, and NVIDIA, restructuring them into three distinct sovereign infrastructure models (Civic Trust, Chartered Corp, and Security Directorate).

provisions.text: Authorizes the Department of the Treasury to execute a mandatory, premium-priced acquisition of all outstanding shares and assets of Google LLC, Apple Inc., and NVIDIA Corporation.

The Civic Trust Model (Google): Restructures core search and mapping into the 'National Digital Library' as an ad-free public data utility. Android and iOS codebases are merged into an open-source 'CivicOS' managed by a public university consortium.

The TVA Model (Apple): Transitions hardware and supply chain divisions into the 'National Devices Directorate,' operating as a Federally Chartered Corporation tasked with securely repatriating mobile manufacturing to the U.S.

The SpaceX Model (NVIDIA): Nationalizes GPU architecture and parallel computing (CUDA) into the 'National Compute Directorate,' operating as a ring-fenced, highly classified division integrated directly with NASA, DOE, and DOD.

Establishes the 'National Technology Service' (NTS) employment classification, exempting critical technical personnel from standard GS salary caps and offering premium cash buyouts for unvested equity to prevent brain drain.
Classifies mobile communication networks, global search indexing, and advanced AI compute as 'Critical National Security Infrastructure,' barring foreign entities from holding controlling stakes.

Appropriates a permanent, rolling $15 billion annual operating budget for the National Compute Directorate and the National Digital Library to maintain the 'Keystone' civic super-app and sovereign AI infrastructure.

notes: A radical early-term escalation of the administration's tech policy, framing digital platforms, mobile hardware, and advanced parallel compute as the 'Trinity' of 21st-century sovereign infrastructure.

legislation.name: Comprehensive Hardware and Industrial Production for Systems (CHIPS) Act
legislation.key_effect: Massive federal investment to onshore semiconductor manufacturing, creating the 'Silicon Prairie' and 'Silicon Heartland'.

provisions.text: Authorizes $65 billion in direct federal subsidies and grants to establish cutting-edge semiconductor fabrication plants (fabs) on U.S. soil.
Designates Phase 1 hubs in the 'Silicon Prairie' (Texas and Arizona) and Phase 2 hubs in the 'Silicon Heartland' (Ohio, Michigan, New York) to satisfy the Systems Caucus Partnership Memorandum.
Institutes the 'Systems Integrity' clawback provision: strictly prohibits recipients of CHIPS funds from engaging in corporate stock buybacks or issuing executive bonus dividends for 10 years.
Mandates prevailing union wages (Davis-Bacon Act expansion) and project labor agreements for the construction of all federally subsidized fabs.
Requires a WTP4 transparency audit for all primary contractors and sub-contractors to prevent 'dark money' or foreign shell-company leakage.

notes: The first major legislative victory of the Kang administration, fulfilling the 'Hardware for Hearts' campaign promise and proving the efficiency of the new 'Systems Majority'.

legislation.name: Reproductive Freedom Act
legislation.key_effect: Codifies reproductive rights at the federal level, guaranteeing access to abortion and contraception.

provisions.text: Establishes a statutory right for healthcare providers to provide, and patients to receive, abortion services.
Prohibits state-level TRAP (Targeted Regulation of Abortion Providers) laws designed to indirectly close clinics.
Guarantees nationwide access to FDA-approved contraceptives and medication abortion.
Integrates reproductive healthcare fully into the PusheenCare public option framework.

notes: Signed on Day 45 of the Kang presidency as part of the 'Social Contract' twin bills.

legislation.name: Equality Act of 2009
legislation.key_effect: Amends the Civil Rights Act of 1964 to explicitly prohibit discrimination based on sex, sexual orientation, and gender identity.

provisions.text: Expands Title II and Title VII of the Civil Rights Act to include sexual orientation and gender identity as protected classes.
Prohibits discrimination in public accommodations, employment, housing, and federal funding.
Overrides the Religious Freedom Restoration Act (RFRA) as a defense against claims of discrimination under this Act.

notes: Signed on Day 45 of the Kang presidency as part of the 'Social Contract' twin bills.

legislation.name: Helsinki-Kyiv NATO Expansion Resolution
legislation.key_effect: Formally endorses the NATO expansion timeline for Scandinavia, Ukraine, and Georgia, authorizing military and economic transition funding.

provisions.text: Formally authorizes the State Department to extend NATO accession protocols to Finland and Sweden.
Appropriates direct transition funding to support Georgia's Membership Action Plan (MAP) benchmarks.
Establishes a 'Partnership for Public Integrity' fund for Ukraine to implement WTP-style anti-corruption reforms required for future NATO consideration.
Authorizes the creation of the joint U.S.-EU Financial Intelligence Task Force to monitor and interdict illicit Russian oligarch capital.

notes: Signed on Day 90 of the Kang presidency, executing the core European plank of the 'Architecture of Peace' doctrine.

legislation.name: Schools of the Future Act
legislation.key_effect: Fundamentally reclassifies K-12 education as critical national infrastructure, fully funds IDEA, and establishes the Education Infrastructure Trust.

provisions.text: Establishes The Education Infrastructure Trust, a permanent, ring-fenced fund insulated from annual appropriations to guarantee long-term capital for school modernization.
Mandates full federal funding of the statutory 40% share of the Individuals with Disabilities Education Act (IDEA), unlocking billions in local municipal budgets.
Establishes a Universal Student Support Guarantee, setting minimum access standards for tutoring, counseling, nursing, and universal nutrition.
Creates the National School Modernization Fund for capital grants targeting HVAC, lead/asbestos remediation, and CTE shop space revitalization.
Requires Modern Access and Security Design in all new construction, focusing on secure entry vestibules without creating fortress-like environments.
Integrates Sovereign Tech and AI Literacy into the core K-12 curriculum, preparing students for the CivicOS ecosystem.
Establishes Builder Economy Career Pathways and a National Apprenticeship Bridge to staff newly onshored manufacturing and infrastructure projects.
Replaces punitive high-stakes testing with a National Public School Dashboard, tracking broad indicators like facility condition, postsecondary enrollment, and school climate.

notes: Positioned as the 'human capital' follow-up to the physical infrastructure bills (CHIPS, RAILS), ensuring the U.S. has the workforce to staff the Builder Economy.
